subject: Operational commitments questionnaire — metrics visibility, alerting, and temporary sampling carveouts
messages:
From: Kate Miller <kate.miller@lumengrid.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lumengrid.com
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational commitments questionnaire for integration (attached)

Hi Jonas —

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement asked us to collect a short operations questionnaire before we finalize the order. I attached LumenGrid's standard procurement form (PDF) — the questions we care most about are under the ‘Operational commitments’ section: how you measure availability and latency, what dashboards/metrics we can see, alerting thresholds and noise reduction, and the process for temporary exceptions during our migration window.

A few clarifying points from our side:
- We expect a 30-day rolling availability number, and p50/p95/p99 latency distributions per route.
- During our initial data migration (3–7 days), we may need temporary sampling or exempted alerting to avoid noisy paging.
- Our security team prefers read-only dashboard access that can be limited to a project scope; if not possible, screenshots + signed attestations are an alternative.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a read-only Grafana link (or equivalent) and the exact definitions for availability and latency you use? Procurement would like a short written response and any attachments by EOD Tuesday PST so we can move to contract review.

Attachments: LumenGrid_OPS_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (fillable)

Best,
Kate Miller
Senior IT Procurement
LumenGrid
kate.miller@lumengrid.com
+1 415-555-2198

From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Kate Miller <kate.miller@lumengrid.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Operational commitments questionnaire for integration (attached)

Kate —

Received, thanks. Attaching a short summary and a dashboard invite stub while we prepare formal answers. High level answers up front so procurement has what it needs for now:

- Availability: we report monthly and rolling-30-day availability as the percent of successful inference requests (HTTP 2xx) over total requests, excluding maintenance windows and customer-approved outage windows. Typical hosted target in our docs: 99.95% monthly for hosted contracts; for Dedicated we publish committed throughput and a latency SLO.
- Latency: we provide p50/p95/p99 for request end-to-end server-side processing, measured at the platform ingress where we stop-readable instrumentation (milliseconds). We also publish tokenized-per-token compute timings separately if you want model-level decomposition.
- Dashboards: we can provide a read-only Grafana-like viewer scoped to LumenGrid’s account and routes, with token-level cost and latency breakdowns. We’ll provision an invite for your security team's read-only access.
- Temporary sampling/exemption: we offer a documented exception process that allows sampling rate adjustments or alert suppression during migration windows. Typically we authorize a short carveout (3–7 days) with explicit start/end times and compensating monitoring to avoid blind spots.

Next steps: we will prepare formal answers in the questionnaire PDF and a live dashboard invite. Proposed time to complete: EOD Monday PST. If that timeline is tight, Marissa can step in to accelerate.

Attaching: redwood_dashboard_invitation.url (provisional invite link)

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Finally, for the exception process, procurement wants an explicit escalation path (who approves, what logs are kept) and whether exceptions are limited to a single burst or can be staged.

Procurement has a hard deadline for a written packet by EOD Thursday PST so they can include it in their governance review. If you need to loop in any additional folks (security or SRE), please do.

Best,
Kate

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Kate Miller <kate.miller@lumengrid.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Operational commitments questionnaire for integration (attached)

Kate — thanks for the clarifying questions. Below are the canonical answers we’ll include in the procurement packet (short, authoritative, and audit-ready). We’ll also attach the completed PDF and a link to the read-only viewer once provisioned.

1) Maintenance window exclusions:
- Planned maintenance: defined in the contract as scheduled events communicated 72 hours in advance (start/end timestamps). These are excluded from availability calculations.
- Automated patching: small in-place patching that does not impact serving (>99% of patches). If patching requires rolling restarts that affect your reserved capacity, we treat that as planned maintenance and exclude the window after notification.
- Emergency maintenance: only used for critical security incidents; treated as an unplanned outage in metrics unless mutually agreed to be excluded in rare cases (requires post-incident review).

2) Latency definition and queuing:
- p50/p95/p99 are computed on server-side request completion timestamps measured at the ingress endpoint after request de-duplication.
- Queuing time caused by autoscaling or transient backpressure is included in the end-to-end latency metric. We also publish a separate queue-time metric and a model-exec-time metric so you can distinguish causes.

3) Exception/temporary sampling process:
- Request: customer raises an Exception Request (email + form) specifying start/end times, rationale, services/routes affected, and compensating monitoring.
- Approval: the PM on-call and an engineering lead must approve; approval emails are kept in the ticket. For enterprise customers we can map approvals to named approvers in the contract (e.g., LumenGrid Ops lead + Redwood SRE manager).
- Limits: exceptions are generally short (3–7 days). For longer staged rollouts we recommend a staged exception plan with overlapping windows and additional telemetry; these require advance agreement and are part of the onboarding MOP.
- Audit trail: all exception requests and approvals are logged in our ticketing system and linked to the metrics snapshot we capture at start/end. We can provide signed attestation post-exception on request.

Next actions we’ll execute today:
- Finalize the completed questionnaire PDF and return it to procurement by EOD Thursday PST.
- Provision the read-only viewer scoped to LumenGrid routes and send a secure invite to the security contact.
- Share a short runbook excerpt describing exception approvals and the dashboard panels we’ll make visible.

If you want an immediate call to walk through the dashboard and the exception flow, we can host a 30-minute session tomorrow morning PST.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Director, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
